correctness.rationale: The complementary semiperimeter variables convert fixed perimeter and side deficit into fixed first and second symmetric moments. Along that one-dimensional constraint set, the divided-difference identity makes the sum of log-transformed side factors strictly increasing with the third elementary symmetric function because the relevant third derivatives are positive. The two possible repeated-root configurations therefore give the exact upper branch and, below the boundary-contact threshold, the exact lower branch. The hyperbolic and spherical L'Huilier formulas then transfer these extrema to area; the spherical perimeter restriction keeps every transformed argument inside the required positive interval.
